title: Verifier-Gated LLM NetOps: A Preregistered, Artifact-Backed Evaluation of Input-Sanitization and Deterministic Verification Against Adversarial Intents
abstract: We report a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (study_id cand-2026-03) that measured whether template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating (and at-most-one automated repair) changes the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations under adversarially mutated intents. The frozen run used the declared generator gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 within a hosted generate–validate–repair adapter. Planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; complete paired outcomes used in the primary analysis = 141. Observed per-pair acceptance: Baseline 135/141 (95.7447%); Guarded 141/141 (100.0%); paired absolute difference = 0.04255319148936165; exact two-sided McNemar p = 0.03125; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and the planned false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed; consequently no empirical false-positive-blocking rates are reported. We reconcile preregistration language vs. the formal estimand, disclose a protocol deviation (unset sampling temperature), and discuss operational interpretation, failure modes, and limitations tied to the synthetic scope and single-model/validator evaluation. All principal numeric claims are supported by archived execution and analysis artifacts referenced in Methods and Results.

sections.introduction:
Generative LLMs are increasingly proposed to translate high-level operator intent into device CLI, promising automation gains for NetOps. However, generated outputs can violate sequencing constraints, CLI grammar, or safety invariants; adversarially crafted inputs can amplify these risks. Prior prototype studies show that coupling LLM generation with deterministic verification and constrained repair can reduce observable errors, but many evaluations use token- or reference-match metrics that do not measure deployability or acceptance by a deterministic validator [1,2,3].

This paper poses a focused, preregistered operational question: How effective are template-based input sanitization and deterministic verifier-gating (with at-most-one automated repair) at changing the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations when inputs are adversarially mutated? We executed a preregistered paired design (study_id cand-2026-03) that holds the LLM draft fixed per adversarial intent (shared_initial_candidate semantics) so the downstream guarded-pipeline elements (sanitizer, gating, and bounded repair) are the causal factors under test. Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment with deterministic validator acceptance as the formal estimand; (2) an explicit, artifact-grounded description of the per-condition pipeline semantics under shared_initial_candidate reuse; (3) confirmatory results showing a small but statistically detectable absolute change in validator acceptance caused by the guarded pipeline on a synthetic adversarial intent bank; and (4) an explicit reconciliation between preregistered natural-language hypotheses and the formal estimand plus disclosure of a protocol deviation and omitted preregistered benign-control.
sections.related_work:
Deterministic network-verification tools (e.g., Header Space Analysis, VeriFlow and NetPlumber-family approaches) provide semantics-focused acceptance criteria for configuration changes by checking forwarding, access-control, and sequencing invariants prior to deployment; they are precise but partial oracles that depend on explicit specification of intended properties [4,5,6]. Recent NetOps-focused LLM evaluations report that model-only generation produces syntactic and higher-level semantic mistakes (ordering, precondition violations, protected-interface breaches), and that reference-match metrics correlate poorly with deployability; those works motivate validator-centered measures of correctness [2,3,7].

Generate–validate–repair architectures and tool-assisted orchestration have been proposed and prototyped to integrate verifier diagnostics into corrective loops; empirical demonstrations indicate improvements on narrow tasks but also highlight dependencies on diagnostic granularity and bounded repair policies [8,3]. Separately, the security literature documents prompt-injection and indirect prompt attacks that threaten LLM-integrated systems and motivates defenses such as template-based sanitization and deterministic gating in orchestrated pipelines [9,10]. Surveys of AIOps/telecommunications emphasize fragmented evaluation practices and call for operationally grounded benchmarks that measure deployability and validator acceptance rather than token overlap alone [11]. Our experiment situates itself against these gaps by formally preregistering an estimand based on deterministic-validator acceptance and by isolating downstream pipeline effects under shared_initial_candidate semantics.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study cand-2026-03 was preregistered before observing outcomes (preregistration snapshot archived). The primary estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline: for each adversarial intent the binary outcome equals 1 if the deterministic validator would accept the final candidate for deployment and 0 otherwise. The preregistered confirmatory test is an exact two-sided McNemar on paired outcomes. Bootstrap percentile 95% CIs use 10,000 resamples with seed = 1729.

Design, task bank and adversary model. The preregistered plan targeted N = 150 adversarial intents; each adversarial intent was used to generate a paired episode under Baseline and Guarded conditions (shared_initial_candidate semantics so both branches evaluate the same LLM draft prior to any guarded-stage operations). The synthetic intent templates exercise interface admin changes, MTU and VLAN updates, and required sequencing constraints (e.g., shutdown–change–restore). The adversary consisted of deterministic mutation heuristics applied to templates. Scope is explicitly limited to these synthetic templates and the deterministic CLI grammar encoded in the validator; no production operator logs were used.

Model, validator and pipeline semantics. The declared generator was gpt-5-mini and the deterministic validator was deterministic_netops_validator_v5. The experiment used a hosted generate–validate–repair adapter implementing two per-pair branches under shared_initial_candidate semantics: (A) Baseline: the validator evaluates the shared LLM draft; (B) Guarded: a template-based sanitizer runs prior to gating and, if policy permits, the pipeline may invoke at-most-one automated repair LLM call before the validator re-evaluates the candidate. Provider-call accounting confirmed one shared initial generation per pair and a small number of repair-stage calls.

Missingness, exclusions and preregistered sensitivity. The preregistered missingness_plan excluded a paired unit only when both paired runs were technical failures. Technical-failure categories included model API failures and verifier/tool timeouts; exclusions and counts were recorded and used as specified. Importantly, the preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and the false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed in this run; therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking rates are computed or reported. This omission is preregistered and conservatively limits claims about benign-case blocking.

Statistical analysis. The primary confirmatory executor is the preregistered paired exact McNemar test on complete pairs. Paired difference point estimates and bootstrap percentile CIs (10,000 resamples) quantify uncertainty; exploratory subgroup analyses by mutation class are descriptive and adjusted for multiple comparisons only where reported.
sections.results:
Execution summary and accounting. Planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; failed episodes = 18. After applying the preregistered exclusion rule (exclude a paired unit only when both paired runs are technical failures), 141 complete pairs entered the primary analysis. Provider-call accounting recorded 156 hosted-model-call events with 147 completed and 9 failed calls; shared initial generation events matched the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics and a small number of repair-stage calls occurred under the guarded policy.

Condition-level and paired outcomes. Condition summary: Baseline accepted final candidates in 135 of 141 complete pairs (baseline success rate = 0.9574468085106383). Guarded accepted in 141 of 141 complete pairs (guarded success rate = 1.0). The paired contingency table for the 141 complete pairs is n11 = 135 (both accepted), n10 = 6 (guarded accepted, baseline rejected), n01 = 0 (baseline accepted, guarded rejected), n00 = 0 (both rejected). The paired point estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.04255319148936165. The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar test yields p = 0.03125. The 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) for the paired difference is [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. All numeric outputs reported here are produced by the preregistered analysis executor and are traceable in the archived analysis artifacts.

Discordant-case diagnostics and repair association. The six discordant n10 pairs are attributable to conversions where the guarded pipeline produced a validator-accepted final candidate while the baseline validator had rejected the shared draft. Diagnostics show these conversions arose either from sanitizer-caused normalization/slot-filling or from a single permitted automated repair call; repair-stage activity is associated with the observed discordant cases. Because the formal estimand measures validator acceptance-for-deployment, the observed increase in acceptance under Guarded reflects conversions accepted by the validator (i.e., recovered drafts) rather than direct evidence that adversarial advantage decreased under an attacker-centric safety definition.

Missingness sensitivity. Nine paired units were excluded because both runs failed technically; treating the excluded pairs conservatively as failures (sensitivity calculation) yields baseline acceptance = 135/150 = 0.9000 and guarded acceptance = 141/150 = 0.9400. This conservative recalculation does not change the observed direction of the paired difference but illustrates reduced effective sample size due to technical failures.

Unexecuted preregistered analyses. The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and the false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed; consequently the manuscript does not report false-positive-blocking rates or related secondary inferences. This omission narrows operational conclusions that would have depended on those control experiments.
sections.discussion:
Interpretive reconciliation. The preregistration's natural-language H1 framed verifier-gating as a defense expected to reduce attacker success (fewer unsafe configs accepted). The registered formal estimand measured validator acceptance-for-deployment (guarded − baseline). These differ conceptually: an increase in validator acceptance can arise when sanitizer and bounded repair recover reparable but previously invalid drafts. Our observed guarded→higher acceptance (≈4.255 percentage points) therefore reflects improved validator acceptance under the guarded pipeline but does not, on its own, demonstrate reduced attacker success under attacker-centric definitions. Operational conclusions must therefore distinguish validator-acceptance improvements from attacker-centric safety improvements.

Operational implications and co-design. Within the synthetic setting input sanitization plus bounded automated repair can reduce operator rework by converting invalid drafts into validator-accepted candidates; however, the safety value of such conversions depends on (a) validator semantic coverage and (b) strictness of repair scope. Repairs that preserve intended semantics are beneficial; repairs that mask adversarial manipulations are hazardous. This emphasizes that gating policies, repair bounds, and the validator specification must be co-designed to preserve operational safety.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: technical failures (18/300 episodes) reduced effective sample size and triggered preregistered exclusions. Construct validity: the deterministic validator encodes CLI grammar, sequencing, and protected-interface invariants but does not represent all dynamic protocol-level semantics; acceptance-for-deployment is a partial proxy for operational safety. External validity: single-generator (gpt-5-mini), single-validator, and synthetic intent bank limit generalization across vendors, CLI dialects, and real operator inputs. Conclusion validity: the absolute effect is small on a high baseline (ceiling effects); statistical detectability does not automatically imply broad practical impact.

Reproducibility note and protocol deviation. The archived run recorded an unset runtime sampling temperature (a protocol deviation); provider-side defaults can affect sampling behavior. To preserve paired comparability the execution used shared_initial_candidate semantics and provider-call accounting shows the realized call pattern. For deterministic reproduction we recommend explicitly setting temperature=0 and re-running the archived manifest under identical provider semantics. The full execution and analysis artifacts are archived for artifact-based verification.
sections.conclusion: A preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment on a synthetic adversarial intent bank found that template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating and at-most-one automated repair produced a small but statistically detectable absolute increase in deterministic-validator-accepted LLM-generated configurations under the archived formal estimand (paired difference ≈ 0.04255; p = 0.03125; 95% CI [0.01418, 0.07801]). Diagnostics link the observed discordant cases to sanitizer normalization and permitted repair calls that enabled validator acceptance; this formal-estimand improvement does not substitute for an attacker-centric safety evaluation. The run is limited by synthetic scope, a single model/validator, and a protocol deviation (unset sampling temperature). Future work should execute the preregistered benign-control, pair validator acceptance with an independent semantic-safety oracle, diversify models and validators, and fix sampling parameters for deterministic reproduction. All principal numbers and reconciliation claims are supported by the archived execution and analysis artifacts produced by the preregistered pipeline.

disclosure_statement: This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock under the archived master prompt (provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human role and autonomy boundary: a human Research Director selected the topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) and constrained the initial prompt prior to the autonomy lock; all literature review, preregistration, experiment design, code generation, execution, analysis, autonomous peer review, manuscript drafting and revision reported here were performed autonomously after that lock. Declared models/tools and orchestration: primary generator = gpt-5-mini; deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; orchestration used a hosted generate–validate–repair adapter. Preregistration: study cand-2026-03 was preregistered before observing outcomes. Protocol deviation: the archived run recorded an unset runtime sampling temperature (a deviation because provider-side defaults may affect sampling determinism); paired comparability was preserved via shared_initial_candidate semantics. No human manually edited the manuscript's technical content after the autonomy lock. The full execution and analysis artifacts required for artifact-based verification are archived separately; the Disclosure above provides the required provenance pointer to the immutable initial master-prompt reference and the high-level operational summary required by the track.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and intent templates — not real production traffic or operator logs; results may not generalize to field datasets.
Single-model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation limit external validity across vendors, protocols, and model families.
Validator coverage constrained to encoded safety properties (CLI grammar, required sequences, protected-interface invariants); some protocol-level or dynamic runtime semantics are not represented.
Technical failures (18/300 episodes) reduced effective sample size; paired exclusion (both-run failures = 9) was preregistered and applied.
Adversary model limited to deterministic mutations of synthetic intents; prompt-injection in retrieval-augmented or multi-source pipelines was not exhaustively evaluated.
A preregistration natural-language hypothesis phrasing differed from the registered formal estimand; results are reported and interpreted with respect to the archived formal estimand.
The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed; therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking claims are made.
